objective: GitHub Actions workflow definitions inside the assessed repository scope must not contain known workflow patterns that materially weaken CI trust boundaries according to the qualified provider and declared coverage.
applies_to: Git repositories containing GitHub Actions workflow definitions
required_evidence: Readable provider assessment covering every workflow definition in .github/workflows, bound to target and Git HEAD

status_semantics.PASS: Provider executes successfully, workflow inventory is reliably established, provider output is parseable, and zero findings exist under the explicitly qualified policy/threshold.
status_semantics.FAIL: Provider executes successfully and one or more qualified findings exist.
status_semantics.BLOCKED: Provider unavailable, source/version identity mismatch, workflow inventory indeterminate, provider execution/output malformed, or target cannot be reliably assessed.

limitations: Only workflow patterns covered by the pinned Zizmor 1.29.0 provider and its default Regular persona are assessed; absence of findings is not proof that CI is secure.

Assessment is limited to .github/workflows/*.yml and *.yaml collected via the provider's workflows-only mode; other CI configuration (Dockerfiles, Terraform, Kubernetes, application SAST, dependency scanning) is out of scope and belongs to other controls.
Network-dependent online audits are disabled (offline mode); findings requiring live GitHub data are not assessed in this slice.
Workflow inventory certainty is required: zero workflows, indeterminate collection, or provider error is BLOCKED, not PASS.
Checksum integrity for this release relies on GitHub-provided asset digest (no separate checksum file is published for v1.29.0); not independent publisher signature verification.
out_of_scope: Whether a discovered workflow weakness is currently exploitable or already remediated.
Runtime CI secret stores, deployment credentials, and cloud data planes.
Dockerfiles, Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, application SAST, and dependency scanning.
Any project or system security verdict; this control emits one scoped evidence record per assessment.
